screen: rail wiring across the whole file
finding: The product's primary navigation — the six-tool rail — is prototyped on Settings boards and almost nowhere else. 39 of 45 Settings frames carry rail-wired hotspots; the rest of the file is Media 8/40, Brand 3/34, Layers 2/18, Shell 2/17, Pages 1/13, Journeys 1/74, and ZERO on Insert, Content, Publish, History, Review, AI, Inspector, Compare, Client sign-off, Notifications, Preview, Canvas and Ecommerce.
evidence: Per-module scan of reactions on frames + descendants, carriers named rail/Insert, rail/Layers, rail/Pages, rail/Media. 1090 cross-module edges across 161 distinct pairs; ~409 of them originate in Settings.
recommend: Wire the rail on one representative board per module at minimum, or extract the rail into a single component instance whose reactions travel with it. Until then, anyone walking the prototype can only navigate from Settings, and the file's own edge counts read as 'Settings is the product hub', which it is not.

finding: Client sign-off is a terminal island: 10 screens, 8 with internal edges, and ZERO outbound cross-module edges. Nothing in the module leads back to the editor, Review, or Publish.
evidence: Cross-module matrix: 'Client sign-off' is the only module in the file with no outbound cross-module pair. Two of its screens are legitimately marked TERMINAL by design (1339:7193, 1339:7186), which accounts for two, not ten.
recommend: Decide where a client lands after approving or requesting changes — the agency's next step is the whole point of the module — and wire it. Check first whether the code already has that transition; if it does, this is design lagging code.

finding: The raw edge matrix reports Settings/S7 as the file's hub (94 edges to Journeys, 80 to Shell, ~39 to each of Pages/Insert/Layers/Media/Content/Brand). That is an artifact of D-X-01, not an IA fact: the counts are the repeated rail instance on 39 Settings boards.
evidence: 39 of 45 Settings frames are rail-wired vs 0-8 elsewhere; the ~39-40 counts to each rail destination match the rail's six buttons across those boards.
recommend: Recorded so the next reader of the edge matrix does not conclude the product is settings-centred. Any future graph analysis should exclude rail-component reactions or count them once per component, not once per instance.

finding: The editor ships a Components authoring surface with its own DETAIL screen, and the Figma file has no Components module at all. 27 sections, none of them Components.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/sidebar/tabs/ComponentsTab.tsx plus sidebar/tabs/component-library/ (9 files incl. ComponentDetailScreen.tsx, ComponentRow.tsx, ComponentIcon.tsx); server/trpc/routers/site-component.ts exposes 8 procedures; the site menu opens it via openLeftPanelToTab("components"). Insert only carries a COMPONENTS row group for PLACING them — authoring, detaching, updating and the detail screen have no board anywhere.
recommend: New section: Components — list, detail, create-from-selection, update-all-instances, detach (already has a confirm in code), and the empty state. This is one of the four doors IA-10 was about, and it is the one with no design at all.

finding: Templates has a 14-file editor surface including a preview modal and an apply-progress overlay, and the only Templates section in the file is a review scratch section (1084:4527, '🔍 REVIEW · Templates + Components'), not a product module.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/sidebar/tabs/templates/ — 14 files incl. TemplatePreviewModal.tsx, ApplyProgressOverlay.tsx, ApplyProgressOverlay.css; server/trpc/routers/templates.ts exposes 8 procedures; first run offers 'Browse templates' (807:4299).
recommend: Promote a real Templates module: browse, filter, preview, apply-with-progress, applied-result, and the failure state. Applying a template is destructive to existing content — that confirm has no board.

finding: Canvas comment mode is a shipping editor feature with a keyboard chord and its own canvas layer, and it has no boards. The Review module covers review THREADS in a panel, which is a different object from a pin dropped on the canvas.
evidence: editor/canvas/comments/CommentLayer.tsx; the entry point is the plain 'C' key (useEditorShortcuts.ts:106) plus a StudioHeader control; server/trpc/routers/comments.ts exposes 5 procedures.
recommend: Board the pin lifecycle: place, typing, posted, replied, resolved, and what a pin looks like to a client in the shared view. A feature whose only entry is an unlabelled keyboard chord is also worth an IA finding in its own right.

finding: server/trpc/routers/forms.ts (5 procedures) has NO editor-side surface, so the absence of a Forms module in the editor file is correct, not a gap.
evidence: grep for FormSection / form-element / FormFieldInspector across editor/inspector and editor/sidebar returns nothing. Forms are a dashboard-side concern.
recommend: No action. Recorded so the next audit does not re-file it — a router without an editor surface is not an editor design gap.
